silhouette.reason: panel-1: The strongest read of these busts: big swept-back pointed ears, bald domed skull and a long hooked nose name a goblin in front and side silhouettes. Weakened by the ears being paper-thin spikes with a ragged tip, the stray wire hairs adding noise, and the vest torso being a boxy block. | panel-2: Big swept ears, hooked nose, bald dome and neckerchief knot name a goblin from the front and 3/4 outline. In side view the ears lie flat against the skull and disappear, the ear tips end in thin ragged needles, and the sparse hairs add noise rather than shape. The torso is a boxy lump. | panel-3: Strongest read of the set: big swept ears, bald dome, hooked nose and scrawny neck name a goblin instantly in front and side silhouette. Weakened by the ears being razor-thin blades from the side and the wispy strand hair adding noise rather than shape.
fixes: Give the ears thickness at the base and a cupped concha so they read as cartilage, not fins
Cut the floating wire hairs to a few tufts that sit on the scalp
Shape the torso with sloped, narrow goblin shoulders instead of a rectangular vest block
Angle the ears back and outward by 25-35 degrees so they read in the side silhouette
Thicken the ear tips and round off the needle ends
Group the white hairs into two or three tufts with a clear shape
Narrow and slope the shoulders into a hunched goblin posture
Give the ears thickness and a curled rim so they hold volume in side view
Group the stray hairs into a few deliberate tufts (crown, behind ears) instead of scattered wires
Hunch the head forward on the neck for a more characterful profile

proportions.reason: panel-1: Goblin caricature mostly works: large cranium, long nose, small chin, wide ears. But the neck is long and thin for the head, the eyes sit shallow and small without heavy lids, the mouth is a narrow slit tucked under the nose with tiny tusks, and the jaw has little structure. Torso is too wide and square relative to a scrawny goblin build. | panel-2: As a stylised goblin the head works: large cranium, big nose, small jaw with lower teeth. Problems: the ear is a thin flat sheet welded along a vertical ridge on the skull with no concha or thickness, the eyes are small and shallow under a soft brow, the mouth is a thin slit with teeth that sit on the lip rather than in a jaw, the back of the skull is a plain sphere and the neck is a smooth tube. The torso is as wide as it is featureless. | panel-3: Cranium-to-face ratio and nose size are appropriately caricatured. But the ears attach too high and too far forward on the skull (root near the temple), eyes are small and shallow without lid thickness, the mouth line is a narrow slot with tiny teeth tacked on, and the neck is a long uniform tube that meets the collar abruptly.
fixes: Shorten the neck and add a forward head-carriage hunch
Enlarge the eyes and add heavy, drooping upper lids and deep orbits
Widen the mouth toward the cheeks and give the underbite visible lower fangs
Narrow and slope the shoulders; reduce torso width ~15%
Rebuild the ear with a thick root, concha bowl and rolled helix, attached at the jaw hinge
Deepen the orbits and add a heavy brow ridge and lids
Open the mouth line and seat the teeth in the lower gum behind the lip
Add occipital bulge, neck tendons and collarbones
Drop the ear root to brow-to-nose height behind the jaw hinge
Recess the eyes and add heavy upper lids and bags for goblin character
Widen the mouth and sculpt an underbite with the teeth seated in a lip line
Taper the neck with visible tendons into the trapezius

materials.reason: panel-1: Skin has a decent olive tone with reddish cheek and ear flush and a subtle sheen, though it reads more rubber than skin. Hair strands render as silver-white wire. Leather vest has some brown value variation, but the cream shirt panels carry dark grey blobs that read as holes in the texture; the red scarf is a smooth tube with no cloth weave. | panel-2: Green skin has some mottling, red on cheeks and ear rims and a mild sheen, which is the best skin of the set; amber eyes read. Leather vest is a brown smear with a faint tooled line pattern, the neckerchief is flat red clay, the shirt is plain cream, and dark grey patches on the sleeve openings read as missing texture. Hairs are white ribbons with black edges. | panel-3: Green skin has some colour variation (red flush on cheeks and inner ear) and the amber eyes read well. Leather vest reads as brown leather by hue but has the same roughness as skin; the red scarf looks like rubber tubing; patches are flat grey-cream decals with black holes that read as missing texture.
fixes: Lower skin specular, add pore-scale roughness and darker crease tint around eyes and nostrils
Make the hair coarse grey-brown with tapered tips instead of shiny white wire
Replace the dark blobs on the shirt with stitched patches or torn holes showing depth
Give the scarf a knitted or woven roughness and flatten its cross-section
Give the leather a grain normal and edge highlights, lower roughness on worn areas
Add a cloth weave and fold shading to the neckerchief and shirt
Fix the dark grey patches at the arm openings: cap them with shirt or skin colour
Remove the black outline on the hair cards (alpha or vertex colour bleed)
Raise leather roughness variation and add edge darkening on the vest
Model the scarf as knotted cloth with folds rather than a rounded tube
Give the patches stitched borders and cloth weave instead of flat holes
Add a wet specular to the eyes and subtle veining on the scalp

Add crow's feet, nasolabial folds, warts and a pore normal to the skin
Add notches, a ring or tears to the ears with real thickness
Model vest edge thickness, stitch rows and eyelets for the lace
Smooth the hair card curves (more segments) and root them in the scalp
Sculpt ear helix/concha and a nick or notch in one ear
Add nostril flare, forehead and crow's-feet wrinkles and a few warts
Add vest lacing, toggles and a belt strap

It stays generic: stains are soft blotches not tied to folds or edges, the cloth is not frayed, and left and right are nearly mirrored. | panel-3: Patched vest and scruffy hair begin to tell a story of a poor scavenger, and the cheek flush adds life. fixes: Add a scar across the brow or a notched ear, dirt under the eyes and in skin creases
Make patches real stitched cloth with edge fraying, and darken grime at vest hems and seams
Stain and fray the scarf ends

Break symmetry: one torn ear, a missing tooth, a scar across one brow
Turn patch holes into sewn-on mismatched fabric with crude stitches
Add grime at the neck, nails-scratched scar on the scalp and a chipped tooth
